text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder calls for Social Democrats to take more critical stance on EMU, make approval conditional
- Parliamentary speaker Rita Suessmuth secures fresh injunction preventing Bild newspaper publishing allegations that she used official flights for private matters
- President Roman Herzog defends continuing imposition of solidarity surcharge
- Consumer sentiment muted for 1997
- Level of federal investment in roads and railways to be maintained in 1997
HANDELSBLATT
- Closed property funds report boom
- SPD's Schroeder irritates own party with call for it to reserve right to veto new single currency
- Institutes fear new record unemployment in 1997
- Mortgage business growing again despite fears
- Ruling coalition wants to push through 12 reform projects by autumn
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bavarian CSU wants to limit immigration of foreigners
- Lemonade manufacturers favour "PET" bottles ahead of glass
- Brewery industry loses ground again
- IG Metall union boss says VW chief executive Piech should apologise to Opel in Lopez affair
DIE WELT
- New controversy breaks out over continuing economic aid to eastern Germany
- Germans less optimistic this year than last, institute says
- SPD's Schroeder causes outrage with call for party to keep veto open on EMU
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
